bug_report_content:
id: 1058
status: Fixed
summary: Template types on methods incorrectly trigger inference of a template on the class if that template type is unknown
labels: ['Type-Defect', 'Priority-Medium']
stars: 0
commentCount: 4
Comment 0 (2013-08-01): See i.e. /** * @constructor * @template CLASS */ var Class = function() {}; /** * @param {function(CLASS):CLASS} a * @template T */ Class.prototype.foo = function(a) { return 'string'; }; /** @param {number} a * @return {string} */ var a = function(a) { return '' }; new Class().foo(a); The CLASS type is never specified. If the @template T line is removed from the foo method, the block compiles with but with the @annotation on the method, the compiler seems to try to infer CLASS from the usage and fails compilation.
Comment 1 (2013-08-03): Thanks for the report.
Comment 2 (2013-10-08): This issue was closed by revision b168c8822b2d.
Comment 3 (2013-10-16): This issue was closed by revision b168c8822b2d.
